# Space Law On Space Station 14, stations operate under abbreviated space law. All crew, passengers, and visitors aboard the station are expected to follow these laws.
Foreign invaders, such as nuclear operatives, ninjas, and pirates, are not protected under space law. Traitors are not foreign invaders, so they are usually protected by space law.
Space Law is not the server rules, but some rules reference Space Law and require it to be followed by certain people or to some degree.
## Treatment of Prisoners Prisoners still have certain rights that must be upheld by law enforcement: - Prisoners must be granted adequate medical care. - Prisoners must be allowed access to basic communications equipment (headsets or radios) so long as they are not abused. - Prisoners must be granted clothing, food, water, shelter, and safety. If the brig is no longer safe, confinement must be established in another location. - Prisoners must be given access to legal counsel during an interrogation if requested and available. - Prisoners must be given their shift-mandated PDA after confinement has finished, unless there is solid proof of PDA tampering. In case of tampering, the PDA is to be secured and replaced with a new unit. - Prisoners must be granted freedom of movement, and should not be restrained with handcuffs or other devices after incarceration unless there is an undue risk to life and limb. Similarly, any prisoners held for Permanent Confinement should be kept in the communal brig rather than in a solitary cell, unless they pose a risk to life and limb.
## Contraband Contraband is a broad category of items that are illegal to possess or use without proper authorization. While there are no existing charges for holding contraband, it is still prohibited and should be taken and secured without proper documentation authorizing usage. There are three general tiers of contraband, and they are governed by the following regulations:
- Minor Contraband: Any contraband which is restricted to a department other than Command or Security is minor contraband unless otherwise specified. The Captain or Head of Security may authorize individual use of minor contraband, and other department heads may authorize its use restricted to their assigned department. - Major Contraband: Any contraband which is restricted to the Command or Security department is major unless otherwise specified. The Head of Security may authorize the use of contraband that is particularly restricted to Security; the Captain may authorize the use of any major contraband. - Highly Illegal Contraband: Highly illegal contraband includes Syndicate contraband and magical contraband. Without explicit authorization from Central Command, highly illegal contraband may only be used in the event of dire, immediate emergencies, and only to prevent death or gross bodily harm. Once the emergency is dealt with, the contraband should be stored in a secure location.
Security is obligated to seize contraband through routine searches or when processing criminals in the brig, but may prioritize other duties over confiscation if they see fit. With regards to contraband usage, Security is expected to follow the same regulations as everyone else. Confiscated contraband should be transferred to the Security department for secure storage or permanently disposed of. Collaborating with Cargo to sell confiscated contraband is highly encouraged, as it generally fetches a high value.
## Search and Seizure A personnel search is the inspection and seizure of a crewmember's possessions. If any contraband is found during a search, the officer should confiscate the restricted items. Non-restricted items may be seized by Security if they were used to facilitate a crime. After the search is conducted, all legal items are to be returned to the person. A crewmate may legally decline any search conducted without probable cause or a warrant while the alert level is green. Random searches without probable cause or a warrant are permitted at any other alert level.
A departmental search is the sweep of an entire area or department for contraband. It is recommended that the officers be extremely thorough, checking all lockers, crates, and doors. These can only be done with permission or, ideally, a warrant signed by the department head or the highest-ranking member of the command staff, usually the Captain.
## Implantation Any prisoner in custody can be subjected to implantation or implant extraction procedures, so long as it's within reason. The process of adding or removing an implant should not prolong the detainee's sentence; you cannot hold them longer to perform the procedure unless stated otherwise. A former inmate may be requested to undergo implantation/extraction at a later time; if the circumstances during their confinement warrant it, they must comply. The following have been listed out with special circumstances; anything not in this list can still be applied, given the proper legal context. A prisoner can still receive implantation/extraction procedures without meeting the circumstances if they give their clear consent.
[color=#a4885c]Tracking Implants:[/color] Trackers can be applied to any suspect that has been convicted of a violent crime (the red crimes with a V suffix).
[color=#a4885c]Mind Shields:[/color] Mind Shields can be administered to any suspect charged with a crime if there is reasonable and articulable suspicion to believe they committed the crime while under mind control. If there is undeniable proof of ongoing mind control on the station, such as a successful deconversion, all the following statements apply:
- Crew can be required to be shielded and may be forcibly implanted if they refuse. - If a suspect refuses to cooperate or the implant fails to function, they can be charged with Refusal of Mental Shielding. - Unlike standard implantation, you may indefinitely extend the duration of a prisoner's sentence until you finish issuing Mind Shields, so long as active attempts are made to procure implants and complete the implantation procedure.
Usage of contraband implanters is a detainable offense, but it's not reasonable to detain someone solely for having an unidentified implant inside them.
## Implant Removal Any prisoner in custody can be subjected to implant extraction for a specific implant if there is reasonable suspicion that they have it implanted. Detainees may not be forced or coerced into performing implant extraction on themselves against their will.
## Sentencing Under Normal circumstances, no sentence longer than 15 minutes may be issued. This includes crimes that may stack up to 20, or even 25 minutes. Officers may arrest and stack crimes as they believe is necessary up until the 15 minute mark.
Use common sense and humanity when issuing punishments. You should not always seek the most severe punishment you can; you don't always have to give the maximum time or look to demote someone. Prisoners cooperating and on good behavior should have their sentences reduced. Always take severity into account and charge only what is needed for someone to learn their lesson.
[color=#a4885c]Crime Stacking:[/color] When sentencing criminals, all crimes commited will be taken into account. These crimes will stack in accordance with their severity. However, discretion is advised for stacking crimes with the intent to achieve a higher sentence. You as an officer are intended to protect, not punish. It is the job of the sentencing officer, and the warden, to ensure that a criminal is charged only with crimes confirmed to aid the most severe crime. When charging in these situations, an officer should take the highest and most severe crime, and sentence stackable crimes in accordance with the highest crime.
- Example: A suspect has broken into security during a sentencing of a prisoner, they then attempt to uncuff the prisoner and let them out of security, but are stopped while doing so. In this instance, they commited a 3-00 (Obstruction of Justice) and a 2-03 (Secure Trespass). The arresting officer in this instance would be able to sentence this prisoner up to 15 minutes max. However, due to the failed nature of the crime, and the fact that the crewmember was subdued without much resistance, the officer is more likely to arrest for only 5 minutes, if any sentence is even chosen to be given. - Example 2: A suspect has broken multiple inmates out of prison, and is now assaulting an officer who is trying to arrest them. In this instance they commited a 4-00 (Breach of Custody) and a 2-04 (Assault). Even if an officer was to max sentence both (a 25 minute total sentence), the max sentence allowed would be 15 minutes, since it is not over 30 minutes total.
Remember, context matters greatly, and maximum sentences should be reserved for the worst offenders.
[color=#a4885c]Repeat Offenders:[/color] A repeated crime occurs when someone is released after committing a crime and then commits the same crime again during the same shift. Repeated crimes can be charged with tacked-on time; first repeat: 3:00, second repeat: 6:00, third repeat: Permanent Confinement. It should be noted that each tacked-on time is directly linked to one charge, and that in the instance of multiple crimes being committed, you should use the longer time for the maximum allowable sentence. For example, if someone does their second repeat of Assault and one count of Kidnapping, their maximum allowable sentence would be 11 minutes. 5 from the Moderate crime of Assault, plus 6 from the second repeat.
[color=#a4885c]Accessory, Attempting, and Intention:[/color] If someone intentionally, knowingly, and substantially assists someone in enacting a crime, they can be charged with the relevant crimes, such as an engineer giving someone tools, who says they are going to break into an area. The same applies to a clear and substantial attempt to commit a crime, or a person who shows clear intent to act out a crime, such as a syndicate nuclear operative arming a nuke but getting arrested before it goes off, they can still be charged with station-wide destruction. ## Normal Punishments - [color=#a4885c]Warning:[/color] For minor crimes, fix the issue, then warn the person not to attempt the crime again. If they still proceed to do it at a later date, sentencing may be preferable. - [color=#a4885c]Confinement:[/color] The typical punishment, being confined in a cell for a temporary amount of time according to the crimes. - [color=#a4885c]Demotion:[/color] Entails removing all departmental gear they have on their person and revoking the involved department access from their ID. This requires the Captain's or the involved department head's approval. Demotions should only be issued if the person poses a threat to their own department or is in a position where they have/can abuse their job's gear to commit further crimes.
## Major Punishments - [color=#a4885c]Permanent Confinement:[/color] Permanent confinement is permitted for when crimes stack past 30 minutes in total time. However, under normal sentencing, no sentence is allowed to be longer than 15 minutes. A permanent confinement may occur only after the 30 minute threshhold may be reached via all stackable crimes commited, repeated offenses, or a capital crime being commited. - [color=#a4885c]Execution:[/color] A humane way of dealing with extremely unruly crewmates. Within reason, a prisoner who has been given the death sentence may pick how they wish to be killed. Common methods are firing line, lethal injection, exile, and high voltage electrocution. Another alternate method of "execution" is the process of placing a staff member's brain into a borg, which is allowed so long as it is lawful. Execution can only be issued with the Captain's or acting Captain's approval; if the HoS is acting Captain or there is no acting captain, all heads of staff are to hold a vote on the matter. - [color=#a4885c]DNR:[/color] A DNR (do not resuscitate) order is an alternative to execution that may be placed on criminals subject to certain conditions. The criminal must be dead before the order is placed, and available Security and/or Medical resources (including personnel) must be in use for other purposes, such as a mass-casualty scenario. The criminal must be eligible for execution, and the DNR must be authorized following the same procedure as an execution.
## Accountability Security and Command are not above the law. Security is expected to follow the law as much as the crew they protect. As a security officer, it is your job to take accountability for the actions of you and your fellow officers. You must follow the law and all proper procedures to the best of your ability. Failure to do so is considered an in-character issue, and will be the duty of the warden to reprimand and appropriately punish. Unreasonable failure, as determined by game admins, of the Captain, HOS, or Warden to ensure space law is followed will be considered a rule issue, not an in-character issue.
It is the Warden, Head of Security, and Captain's job to ensure that all officers are appropriately sentencing prisoners in accordance with security guidelines. The Captain, Head of Security, and Warden are responsible, within reason, for ensuring that security officers issue appropriate sentences that comply with Space Law. If they are aware of an inappropriate sentence, including an excessively long one, and there is no urgent threat or danger to prioritize, they must work to correct it. Additionally it is the Warden's job to issue punishments to offending officers for breaking Security guidelines. Sufficient abuse of power or incompetence should result in demotion.
